verdicts.rationale: The reported defect claims that POST /collections/{name}/points/query accepts a nonexistent lookup_from.collection and returns HTTP 200, which it characterizes as a Type1_IllegalSuccess violation. However, analysis of the source code reveals that collection validation for lookup_from DOES exist (lib/collection/src/common/fetch_vectors.rs:264) but only executes in the code path that resolves referenced point IDs. The test query in output_qdrant_016.log used raw vectors with no ID references, so the lookup_from.collection field was never accessed and the validation code never executed. The API correctly returned 200 with results from the source collection because it successfully executed the query using the provided raw vector without needing to access the lookup_from collection. This is by-design behavior: lookup_from is an optional parameter for cross-collection ID lookup, validated only when IDs from that collection are actually referenced. The defect report misunderstood the lazy validation design as a missing validation bug. To trigger the actual validation, the query would need to reference point IDs from the lookup_from collection via prefetch queries or Nearest(VectorInputInternal::Id), at which point the 404 Collection {name} error would be returned.
